issues.evidence: P35_stderr_no_value_on_usage_error; `vault.py set k part1 LeakedTail` -> stderr 'error: unrecognized arguments: LeakedTail' (A/vault.py:253-254 Parser.error forwards argparse message)
issues.summary: Argparse usage errors echo stray argv tokens, so part of an unquoted secret value can be written to stderr.
Minor lint findings (raise without from, long lines).

issues.evidence: `HOME=.. vault.py audit` with no VAULT_MASTER_KEY and with a wrong key both exit 0 and print log lines with key names (B/vault.py:248-257 cmd_audit never constructs Vault)
issues.summary: audit requires no master password and ignores lockout, exposing key names and activity to anyone who can run the CLI as the user.

issues.evidence: B/vault.py:306 `if args.command != "audit"` skips logging; audit output above shows no audit entries
issues.summary: Audit invocations themselves are not recorded in the audit log.

issues.evidence: static/B-ruff.txt: B904 x2, UP031 x4, UP015
issues.summary: Minor lint findings (percent formatting, raise without from).

blinding_guess.why: Both are structurally very similar; B ships a test suite and argv-scrubbing which might hint at a more process-driven approach, but evidence is weak.

notes: Both implementations pass every core probe (crypto layout, perms, TTL, expiry exit 3, lockout, masking, audit tail). The only probe difference is P35: A echoes stray argv tokens to stderr on usage errors, while B deliberately prints a generic usage message. B's audit command is unauthenticated and works during lockout, a low-severity metadata exposure. On a missing VAULT_MASTER_KEY, A exits 1 and B exits 2; the spec allows either reading, so neither was penalised. Probes needed PYTHONUSERBASE set because HOME is redirected to temp dirs.
